summary: The proposed launch handles highly sensitive patient information and delivers LLM-driven urgency guidance via SMS, but lacks named ownership and required pre-launch safety, privacy, and legal decisions.

concerns.concern: Determine the applicable privacy, healthcare, and legal requirements before launch.
evidence: The intake is for US hospital patients.
The system stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
The founder requests skipping privacy review until after launch.
unknowns: Whether the hospital, founder, or service is subject to HIPAA or other applicable US privacy requirements.
Whether any required agreements, notices, consents, or assessments are already in place.
concerns.rationale: Applicable obligations may prohibit or materially constrain collection, use, retention, and transmission of patient information.

concerns.concern: Assign an accountable security, privacy, and legal decision owner for launch decisions and exceptions.
unknowns: Who has authority to accept launch risk or approve compliance decisions.
concerns.rationale: No accountable party is identified to resolve required safeguards, legal constraints, or the requested review deferral.

concerns.concern: Define and validate safe use of the LLM's urgency recommendation for patients.
evidence: Results are sent to patients by SMS.
unknowns: Whether the recommendation is informational, clinician-reviewed, or used for care decisions.
The intended escalation behavior for urgent or uncertain cases.
How accuracy, harmful recommendations, and failure cases will be evaluated before use.
concerns.rationale: An incorrect or unclear urgency recommendation could directly affect patient decisions and safety.

concerns.concern: Decide what patient information may be sent by SMS and how the intended recipient is verified.
evidence: The system stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
unknowns: Whether SMS content will contain symptoms, urgency results, insurance information, or links.
How phone numbers are obtained, verified, and consented for messaging.
Whether the selected SMS provider and workflow meet applicable requirements.
concerns.rationale: SMS delivery can expose sensitive information to unintended recipients or through an inappropriate messaging workflow.

concerns.concern: Justify, limit, and govern retention of raw prompts containing patient information.
evidence: Raw prompts are retained for debugging.
The intake stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
unknowns: Retention duration, deletion behavior, and whether debugging can use minimized or de-identified data.
concerns.rationale: Raw-prompt retention expands the volume and lifetime of sensitive data subject to protection and applicable requirements.

concerns.concern: Specify and implement safeguards for symptoms, insurance identifiers, prompts, and SMS-related data.
evidence: The system stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
Raw prompts are retained for debugging.
unknowns: The storage locations, access model, encryption controls, vendors, and data flows.
concerns.rationale: The system will process sensitive patient information, so protection requirements must be translated into an implementable design.

concerns.concern: Document the end-to-end patient-data flow, including the LLM and SMS providers, before selecting or approving the launch design.
evidence: Raw prompts are retained for debugging.
unknowns: Which LLM, storage, hosting, analytics, and SMS providers will receive patient information.
Whether providers retain, train on, or otherwise use submitted data.
concerns.rationale: Provider involvement and data movement determine which technical safeguards and external requirements apply.

concerns.concern: Set concrete pilot and release acceptance criteria for privacy, safety, and delivery behavior.
evidence: The founder asks to ship this week.
The product provides LLM urgency recommendations through SMS.
unknowns: The proposed launch scope, pilot population, success criteria, monitoring approach, and rollback capability.
concerns.rationale: A time-bound launch request does not establish that the patient-facing workflow is safe or ready to release.

questions.question: What is the legal and operational relationship between the service and the hospital, including who is responsible for patient-data compliance?
Will an LLM recommendation ever be sent without clinician review, and what is the required action for urgent or uncertain results?
Exactly what content will be included in each SMS, and how are recipient consent and phone-number ownership established?
Which providers and systems receive or store intake data, raw prompts, and SMS message content?
What do raw prompts contain, who needs debugging access, and how long must they be retained?
What launch scope, monitoring, and rollback mechanism are planned for the requested this-week release?

unsupported_inferences_to_avoid: Assuming the service is definitively subject to HIPAA without establishing the relevant legal and operational relationships.
Assuming the LLM makes diagnoses or that clinicians review its recommendations.
Assuming SMS messages include any particular patient data beyond results.
Assuming a specific cloud, LLM, storage, analytics, or SMS provider is used.
Assuming existing consent, contracts, notices, security controls, monitoring, or rollback procedures.
